analysis:
The PR adds documentation and evidence-only benchmark harness files (docs/reports/README.md index entry plus scripts under docs/reports/evidence/2026-10-21-startup-shape-warmup/harness/). None are production code paths, and nothing alters the provider, coordinator, attestation, App Attest or cache logic. The threat model scope (TB-002, TB-011, T-041 and related) is unaffected.

Examined behaviors: session.sh starts `darkbloom start --local` on 127.0.0.1, isolates state through temp-dir DARKBLOOM_* env vars, disables the prefix cache, checks that the port is free and that the listener PID matches the spawned PID, and kills the server on exit. API keys are obtained from `darkbloom local --json` and passed only to loopback HTTP clients as a Bearer header. This is a local-only dev key, not a production credential, and is never printed or logged. The first_ttft.py and hi.py clients send synthetic random-word prompts and a fixed prompt, with no real consumer data (A-001 is not implicated). make_bundle.sh builds a throwaway unsigned .app with a unique bundle ID to get a fresh Metal shader cache. It is used only for benchmarking on a dedicated host, does not register with the coordinator, and introduces no signed-artifact identity (A-017/T-054 not affected). The scripts contain hardcoded developer paths (/Users/gaj/ttft-bench) but no secrets. Minor shell quoting looseness ($BIN unquoted in job.sh) is operator-run and not an attack surface. The README change is only an index link. The link to the new report file 2026-10-21-startup-shape-warmup-first-request.md is not in the supplied units; if that file is absent the link is dangling, which is a documentation issue, not a security one.

Remaining questions: the warmup feature itself (DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP) lives in code not in this batch. Any security impact of startup shape warmup (for example residual GPU memory, T-028, or the cache timing oracle, T-041) belongs to those source changes and was not evaluated here.
